word.meaning: to know (a person, place or thing)
word.shortDefinition: To be familiar with someone or something.

intro.title: Two ways to know
paragraphs: English has one verb, 'know'. German has two, and they're not interchangeable. Kennen means knowing someone or something because you've met it. Wissen means knowing a fact.
Ich kenne Anna: I know Anna. Ich weiß, wo Anna wohnt: I know where Anna lives. Getting this right is one of the clearest signs of a learner who's past the first weeks.

etymology.title: Where it comes from
etymology.summary: Kennen shares an ancient root with English 'know' and 'can'. In Scotland the word survived almost unchanged.

cognates.note: I dinnae ken: I don't know
'beyond my ken': outside what I know

bonus.meaning: to get to know, to meet
bonus.note: Freut mich, Sie kennenzulernen: pleased to meet you.

tables.title: kennen and wissen side by side
tables.intro: Kennen is regular. Wissen is irregular in the singular.
notes: Ich weiß and er weiß are the same, with no -t on er weiß.
Kennen is followed by a noun. Wissen is usually followed by a clause: dass, wo, wie, wann, ob.

wordFamily.english: to get to know, to meet

keyTrap.title: The big trap: kennen or wissen?
keyTrap.explanation: Ask yourself: is it a person, place or thing I've met? Use kennen. Is it a fact or the answer to a question? Use wissen.

wrong.verdict: Where he lives is a fact, so it needs wissen.

commonMistakes.title: I don't know
commonMistakes.explanation: The everyday 'I don't know' is about a fact, so it's wissen.

commonMistakes.title: Meeting someone
commonMistakes.explanation: For meeting someone for the first time, German uses kennenlernen.

examples.german: Wir haben uns im Kurs kennengelernt.

sampleSentences.german: Ich kenne ein gutes Restaurant in der Nähe.
sampleSentences.english: I know a good restaurant nearby.

sampleSentences.german: Weißt du, wann der Zug kommt?
sampleSentences.english: Do you know when the train is coming?

quiz.prompt: Ich ___ nicht, wie spät es ist.
quiz.fullAnswer: Ich weiß nicht, wie spät es ist.
quiz.explanation: A fact, followed by wie: wissen.
Where the station is is a fact: wissen.

memoryHook: Kennen is who and where you've met. Wissen is what you've learned. Ich kenne Anna, ich weiß ihre Nummer.
